drivingQuestion: Where must one who erred in reciting Shema, not knowing where he erred, resume?
outcomeNote: R' Yoḥanan's qualification stands unchallenged; the narrative frame closes with the two sages' appreciation.

segments.he: רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי הֲווֹ קָא קָטְרִין לֵיהּ גְּנָנָא לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר. אֲמַר לְהוּ: אַדְּהָכִי וְהָכִי אֵיזִיל וְאֶשְׁמַע מִלְּתָא דְבֵי מִדְרְשָׁא, וְאֵיתֵי וְאֵימָא לְכוּ. אֲזַל אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לְתַנָּא דְּקָתָנֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
segments.en: With regard to an error in the recitation of Shema, the Gemara recounts: «Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi were once tying a wedding canopy» in preparation «for» the wedding of «Rabbi Elazar. He said to them: In the meantime,» until you finish, «I will go and hear something in the study hall, and I will come and say it to you. He went and found the tanna» who recited mishnayot in the study hall, «who was reciting» this Tosefta «before Rabbi Yoḥanan:»

segments.he: קָרָא וְטָעָה וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְהֵיכָן טָעָה, בְּאֶמְצַע הַפֶּרֶק — יַחְזוֹר לָרֹאשׁ. בֵּין פֶּרֶק לְפֶרֶק — יַחְזוֹר לְפֶרֶק רִאשׁוֹן. בֵּין כְּתִיבָה לִכְתִיבָה — יַחְזוֹר לִכְתִיבָה רִאשׁוֹנָה.
segments.en: «One who recited» Shema «and erred, and does not know where» exactly «he erred;» if he was «in the middle of a paragraph» when he realized his error, «he must return to the beginning» of the paragraph; «if» he was «between one paragraph and another» when he realized his error but does not remember between which paragraphs, «he must return to the first» break between «paragraphs.» Similarly, «if one erred between writing and writing,» i.e., between the verse: “And you shall write them on the door posts of your house and on your gates” (Deuteronomy 6:9) in the first paragraph and the identical verse (Deuteronomy 11:20) in the second paragraph, «he must return to the first writing.»

segments.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁלֹּא פָּתַח בִּ״לְמַעַן יִרְבּוּ יְמֵיכֶם״, אֲבָל פָּתַח בִּ״לְמַעַן יִרְבּוּ יְמֵיכֶם״ — סִרְכֵיהּ נָקֵט וְאָתֵי.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him: They only taught» this halakha in a case «where one did not» yet «begin: “In order to lengthen your days”» (Deuteronomy 11:21) which follows that verse at the end of the second paragraph. «However, if he» already «began» to recite: «In order to lengthen your days,» he can assume that «he assumed his routine and continued» and completed the second paragraph.

segments.he: אֲתָא וַאֲמַר לְהוּ. אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אִלּוּ לֹא בָּאנוּ אֶלָּא לִשְׁמוֹעַ דָּבָר זֶה — דַּיֵּינוּ.
segments.en: Rabbi Elazar «came and told» Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi what he heard. «They said to him: Had we come only to hear this, it would have been sufficient.»
